title: Look for seams in the field grassland after Daniel's edit
tier_reason: His brush crossed the tile's own edges on a sheet the game repeats everywhere, so the field may now show a grid.
ask: Landed without Daniel: “Read Daniel's hand edit to Field Grassland”. His brush crossed the tile's own edges on a sheet the game repeats everywhere, so the field may now show a grid.
first_action: Render a frame of the field filled with assets/sprites/generated/terrain_field.png and inspect tile boundaries; also compare the nine 16x16 cells of that 48x48 file against each other and report how far they now differ, and whether cell (16,16,16,16) — the only one farm.gd draws — still wraps edge-to-edge.
source_message: Landed without Daniel: “Read Daniel's hand edit to Field Grassland”.
result: Rechecked the field grassland against the actual renderer. The game cycles all nine 16×16 cells of terrain_field.png by world coordinate; it does not draw only the centre cell. All nine cells are distinct. Across 36 cell pairs, 8–35 of 256 pixels differ (mean 20.83). In the retained 9×9-tile render, I see mild three-tile repetition but no hard grid. Repeating only the centre cell looks more regular, so copying it into all nine positions is not justified. The render, method, boundary-contrast measurements, and limits are in docs/evidence/field-grassland-seam-check.md. No game asset was changed.
